title: Signed error bands gave narrower ranges and higher coverage for 19 Swiss spring plant phases in 2015-2024
abstract: We tested uncertainty ranges for published climate-response fits, using annual statistics for Swiss plants and British butterflies. Models fitted through 2004 used observed target-year weather. We used 2005-2014 errors for calibration and tested 2015-2024. Nominal 90% symmetric bands covered 88.6-91.1% of outcomes in four response groups. Thus the test did not show a broad coverage failure. For 19 spring plant phases, rolling signed-error bands at nominal 80% covered 83.2%, compared with 75.8% for symmetric bands. Mean width fell from 11.10 to 9.67 days. Mean scaled interval score fell by 0.301 (two-year block interval -0.480 to -0.086). An older fitted panel gave the same direction. This shows that a shift in the error centre can improve uncertainty ranges without widening them. Spring climate bands also had lower score than bands based on the old mean or a linear trend. Butterfly and later-plant results were mixed. This is an exploratory secondary test of known data, with ten main test years, shared year effects, changing site coverage and observed weather. It does not validate an operational weather service or guarantee conditional coverage. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes and an independent arithmetic check are included.

display.caption: Later coverage of nominal 90% bands and score of rolling 80% bands. Models use observed target-year weather. Lower interval score is better.

citations.reason: Published annual aggregate statistics; new interval analysis, not new observations.
Earlier driver-information test; we test response uncertainty with observed weather.
Adaptive calibration under distribution shift is established; we do not claim a new conformal theorem.
